diagnosis.original_evidence: The already installed R64 DrawDest eagerly calls ID3DXSprite::Flush for every queued +TIME Draw, while BeforeQueueNode and BeforeQueueEnd and StageExtensionLeave already guarantee exact finite GPU submission boundaries for the same stage owner.
source_trace: Six original +TIME E8 source edges enter and leave StageExtension scope and tag deferred nodes with StageExtensionTime.
The D3DX Sprite owner keeps PendingScope and PendingProducer throughout a homogeneous Begin/Draw buffer.
BeforeQueueNode flushes on stage transition, BeforeQueueEnd flushes the last stage batch and StageExtensionLeave flushes direct glyph batches before restoring source ownership.
R84 downstream Draw hooks transform the GPU-submitted render state into left/right stereo eye paths.
alternatives_rejected: Do not add a global Flush after every stage or suppress D3DX sprites, and do not remove GOAL's separate eager Draw path.
diagnosis.root_cause: The per-Draw stage Flush unconditionally fragments a single homogeneous D3DX owner batch into individual submissions, duplicating GPU synchronization work already bounded by queue/direct source exits.
diagnosis.eye_ownership: The D3DX GPU Draw executes before its exact semantic owner is popped, so the existing R84 per-eye submission can retain ScreenHud provenance. Physical stereo effect remains untested.
